newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bonds drag Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bonds drag Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: AORD 2244.60 -12.10 DJIA closed
SPI futures 2236 -18 US 30yr closed
10yrbond futs 91.730 -0.170 Gold (NY cl) closed
*Shares end weaker, dragged down by bonds after strong retail figures. Total volume 240.56 million shares, value A$583.73 million, 964 stocks traded, 305 steady, 284 rises, 375 falls

The Australian share market closed lower on Tuesday, dragged down by a battered bond market that had its hopes for further local interest rate cuts dashed by much stronger than expected July retail data.
Speculation of a larger than expected rate hike by the U.S. Federal Reserve also depressed bond market sentiment.

At 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 12.1 points lower at 2,244.6, while September share price index futures were 18 points down at 2,236 and at an 8.6 point discount to the underlying index.

With bonds caught in the crossfire of static local rates and possibly higher U.S. rates and with Wall Street closed for the Labor day holiday, brokers said the local bourse had provided no incentives for buyers.
"It's taken a bit of a dive but turnover has been reasonably quiet with the U.S. markets closed," said senior dealer at Nevitts Ltd, Jim Tredenick.
"There was some buying early but it drifted off for the rest of the day and I put that down to the retail figures."
While turnover was at reasonable levels, brokers said this belied a day of essentially slow activity.

While the bourse's closing bell coincided with the launch of U.S. cruise missiles against Iraq, brokers said the potential of the conflict had been largely ignored as other factors were the driving forces in the market.
"Our market has weakened on the Wall Street Journal article suggesting that the Fed is about to move," said Eric Gale, head of institutions at Ord Minnett.
The article suggests that the U.S. Federal Reserve may move to tighten rates by 0.5 percentage points unless it saw more conclusive evidence of a slowdown in U.S. growth.
The results season continued, albeit at a slower pace thanm recent days.
Engineering group ANI was first off the rank, reporting a full year net loss of A$213.19 million and seeing its shares end a cent lower.
Property developer Mirvac saw its shares end just firmer after a higher full year net profit of A$A$21.75 million.
FAI Insurances ended just easier despite a return to profit, its year net profit A$10.04 million, while National Foods ended up after a 39.7 percent higher year net profit of A$15.05 million.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about four to three, while about 32 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, bonds and bills were sold off as hopes of a local rate cut were dashed by stronger than expected July retail data. By 4.35 p.m. (0635 GMT), the 10 year T-bond yield had spiked to 8.30, up 0.18 from monday.

The Australian dollar edged higher as the market absorbed the July retail data and the prospects of a U.S. interest rate hike. Traders said the Iraq crisis was unlikely to prompt real safe haven demand. By 5.25 p.m. (0725 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7916/21.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - SPI futures were active, following bond and bill futures down as interest rate jitters overtook markets.
Options markets also saw good activity as players covered positions ahead of possible further weakness in the U.S. as it resumes after the Labor Day weekend.
